a2_move_rn_anind.reason: gap=+2 (manual=4, measured=6), r/p/w clean. This RTL's own plain-write BIU dispatch has a shared, EA-mode-independent ~6-clock floor -- confirmed exact for CLR.L (a0) (manual=6 including its own explicit cea((An))=2 addition, measured=6). MOVE Rn,(An)'s own manual row is self-contained at NCC=4 with NO cea/fea addition (unlike CLR's row), implying real 68030 microcode genuinely executes MOVE's own EA-then-write sequence 2 clocks faster than CLR's -- a genuine per-instruction microcode difference this project's shared, uniform write-dispatch path can't distinguish. Can't be fixed by shrinking the shared floor (would break CLR's own currently-exact measurement) or via dec_internal_stall_ticks_fixed (that mechanism only applies to register-only, non-bus-touching instructions) without a genuinely new, instruction-specific dispatch-latency mechanism -- same architectural-ceiling character as the briefidx cases above
